Revised assessment incorporating SLOOS and the November 2017 Beige Book: The FOMC’s December 2017 statement highlights solid growth, strong labor markets, and sub-2% inflation with a gradual tightening path. Beige Book insights through mid-November reinforce a moderately positive backdrop: districts reported modest-to-moderate overall growth; labor markets were tight with notable wage increases in professional, technical, and production roles; consumer spending was steady in retail with an upbeat holiday outlook, though auto sales were more mixed. Hurricane-related rebuilding boosted construction activity and raised materials costs, pointing to some emerging price pressures. These Beige Book signals partially offset the more cautious October SLOOS, which showed tighter consumer credit terms and softer loan demand across several categories. Netting these, the outlook remains slightly positive, with wage and activity support outweighing but not eliminating credit- and demand-related caution.
